candidates.title: PRT journal signs a large leaf proof above the node's default RPC fee cap (geth/reth --rpc.txfeecap 1 ether) although a fee under it would be included, never publishes it, reports nothing, and stores a new full candidate every bump interval
candidates.component: PRT transaction journal (doc/recipes/prt-transactions.lua) used by the PRT bridge (doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:attempt/tick)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... | Support'); it stands in for the honest operator's 'Submitting transactions' step (THREAT_MODEL section 2, honest operator's path)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-transactions.lua methods:fees (140-154: fee = min(2*base + priority, max_fee), bumps of 15% from the previous candidate), methods:submit (192-211 ceiling/held path, 236 gas = 2*estimate, 271-298: the candidate is stored before publication and a publication error is returned as published=true with publication_error), M.new defaults (max_fee 100 gwei); doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:report_blocked (573-588: only result.blocked is reported) and methods:tick (770-772: a refused publication counts as published)
candidates.description: The journal chooses a candidate's max fee as min(2*base + tip, max_fee) and raises it by at least 15% every bump_blocks, without regard to the total fee gas*maxFeePerGas. geth and reth refuse in eth_sendRawTransaction, before the pool, any transaction whose gas*maxFeePerGas exceeds --rpc.txfeecap (default 1 ether): geth internal/ethapi SubmitTransaction -> checkTxFee(tx.GasPrice() = GasFeeCap, gas, 1.0). The journal treats that refusal like an ambiguous publication: submit returns {published = true, publication_error = -32000}, the bridge returns 'published', report_blocked reports nothing (the result has no 'blocked' field), and after bump_blocks it signs, stores and publishes a candidate with fees 15% higher, which the node refuses again. When the bump passes max_fee, fees() returns nil, the 'held' search finds no candidate the node holds (all were refused), so the next candidate is signed at fresh fees again (min(2*base+tip, max_fee)), which is again over the cap. The cycle repeats every bump_blocks for as long as the job is due. A winLeafMatch for a large input (an adversary-chosen 64 KiB InputBox input, at its delivery transition) has a gas limit of about 2 * 6.3 M = 12.6 M (Dave's own Gas.WIN_LEAF_MATCH allocation is 5.536 M of execution), so its fee cap is 1 ether / 12.6 M = 79 gwei. For any base fee between about 39.5 and 78 gwei, base + tip fits under the cap and the transaction would be accepted and included, but the journal's first choice 2*base + tip (>= 80 gwei) and every later choice exceed it, so the honest leaf proof is never published while its clock runs. Above 49.5 gwei every fresh candidate is at max_fee (100 gwei, 1.26 ether). Each refused attempt also adds a full candidate (calldata 'data' plus signed 'raw', about 2 x 190 KB of hex for a 94 KB leaf proof) to journal.json, which is rewritten whole and fsynced before each publication, and receipt() queries every candidate of the job on each attempt, so the journal grows by about 380 KB per bump interval for the rest of the job's window.
candidates.trigger: No adversary action is strictly required beyond the honest operator's node running geth or reth with its default --rpc.txfeecap, and a base fee in the band above; an adversary makes it reachable by sending a 64 KiB input (section 7: 'payloads chosen to maximize the honest operator's cost') and steering a match to that input's delivery transition (section 7: 'Steer the dispute to any position'), so that the honest winLeafMatch needs a gas limit above 10 M. Base fees in the 40-80 gwei band occur on Ethereum L1 during congestion; an adversary can also raise them by filling blocks ('Raise activity on the chain'), at a cost.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template on an L1 deployment whose operator node uses the geth/reth default fee cap: the leaf-match position and input size are adversary-chosen, the gas limit is 2 x eth_estimateGas, and the max fee follows the chain's base fee. Smaller leaf proofs (gas*100 gwei <= 1 ether, i.e. gas <= 10 M) never reach the cap with the default max fee.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger is a default policy of the operator's own node plus a base-fee level and an adversary-chosen input and position; none of the section 8 exclusions (machine API misuse, A1-A8 violations, non-guaranteed directories, deep reorgs, host faults that the emulator turns into nothing wrong) covers it. A reviewer may argue the node's fee cap is operator configuration ('trusted by the honest operator ... the operator's host, keys, and node'); trust in the node does not make its documented default policy disappear, and the journal's own --max-fee default (100 gwei) invites totals above it.

2. Role: the journal and bridge are Support per AUDIT.md ('The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... | Support. No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI.'). They implement the honest operator's 'Submitting transactions' (section 2). Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'.

3. High/Medium cases: in the stood-in honest role the defect is not one of the listed High/Medium cases (it is not about unreachable states, constant-factor costs of an R12 emulator operation, or a crash on optional data).

4. Critical (in the stood-in role): R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks.' The honest leaf proof is never submitted while a fee the node and the chain accept exists, so the honest claim can lose the leaf match by timeout (Completeness failure, section 1: 'cannot respond in time. If the honest claim is eliminated, a dishonest claim can win.'). The per-attempt candidate growth also conflicts with R12 'keeping and persisting its own records, ... has a bounded cost per input, per yield, and per match' only weakly (it is bounded by the job's window). Hence Critical in the honest role, so Medium for the support component.

5. Low alternative: if the node's fee cap is read as operator configuration that the goal's premise ('the chain includes its transactions within the dispute clocks') or the operator's fee budget covers, it is Low. Deciding facts: whether the recipe's documented setup targets geth/reth defaults, and whether a node policy that refuses a transaction counts as the chain not including it.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support standing in for a Critical R4 violation) / Low (if the node's fee-cap policy is treated as operator configuration)
candidates.threat_to_goal: The goal assumes the honest operator's transactions reach the chain within the clocks. Here the journal itself picks fees the operator's node refuses, keeps refusing for the whole leaf clock while a valid lower fee exists, and reports no anomaly, so the honest winLeafMatch never reaches the chain; the dishonest claim then wins the leaf match by timeout and can settle a wrong state.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r9/SUBJOURNAL/feecap.lua against a private anvil 1.5.1 (port 28911, manual mining, stopped afterwards). chain.publish was wrapped to refuse exactly like geth's checkTxFee with a 1-ether cap (anvil itself has no cap). The intent called a gas-burning contract so eth_estimateGas gave about 6.32 M (gas limit 12,642,382, like a 64 KiB-input leaf proof). With base fee 40 gwei for 90 blocks: first candidate max_fee 81 gwei (1.024 ether), 30 publications all refused by the cap, 0 accepted, account nonce still 0, 30 candidates stored at nonce 0 (fees cycling 81 -> 93.15 -> fresh 81 ...), no 'blocked' result (so no anomaly), while (base + 1 gwei tip) * gas = 0.518 ether is under the cap. Control at base 38 gwei: first max fee 77 gwei (0.973 ether), all 90 published and mined.
candidates.test_idea: Disposable anvil with manual mining. Wrap chain.publish to return {code=-32000, message='tx fee ... exceeds the configured cap (1.00 ether)'} when gas*max_fee > 1 ether (geth's default rule). Submit a job whose estimate is about 6.3 M gas (gas burner contract) at a fixed base fee of 40 gwei, mining one block per tick for 30 blocks. Required behavior: the job is published and mined at nonce 0 within the window (the node and the next block accept max_fee <= 79 gwei), or, at minimum, the journal reports a blocked/anomaly result and does not store a new candidate per refused attempt. On audit/prt2 it exits 1: nothing is accepted and 10 candidates accumulate.

candidates.title: PRT journal discards every signed attempt when any block arrives during submit, so on chains whose block interval is shorter than one submit (sub-second EVM chains, or remote RPC latency) the honest bridge rarely or never publishes
candidates.component: PRT transaction journal (doc/recipes/prt-transactions.lua methods:submit) called by the PRT bridge (prt-bridge.lua methods:attempt)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes), standing in for the honest operator's 'Submitting transactions'
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-transactions.lua methods:submit lines 161-163 (block = latest at entry) and 266-270 ('local _, current_hash = self.chain:head(); if current_hash ~= block.hash ... then return { waiting = true } end'); doc/recipes/prt-transactions-test.lua 365-378 asserts this behavior; crisium.lua 361-381 (a non-published result waits for the next tip)
candidates.description: submit samples the latest block at entry and, after about ten sequential RPCs (nonce, receipts of every candidate of the job, eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas, eth_call of the full action, eth_estimateGas, which itself executes the call many times, eth_getBalance) and two cast processes (sign, decode-transaction), discards the whole attempt if the latest block hash changed at all, even when the job's window is still open at the new tip and the observation is still canonical. Nothing is stored or published, and crisium retries only at the next tip, where the race starts again. The window and canonicality are already rechecked, so the strict equality is not needed for safety (a stale publication can at worst revert). Whenever the block interval is shorter than one submit, essentially no attempt survives: the honest bridge never publishes any move. When the interval is comparable to the submit latency, each publication (first transaction or fee bump) needs a geometric number of blocks.
candidates.trigger: Deployment on an EVM chain whose block interval is below the submit latency (for example a 250 ms or sub-second chain, or a 1-2 s chain reached through a remote provider with 50-100 ms round trips and a heavy eth_estimateGas for a leaf proof). No adversary action is needed; heavier calls (leaf proofs, chosen by the adversary's steering) make the submit longer.
candidates.reachability: Reachable on any chain where a block can arrive during submit; the probability per attempt is about submit_latency / block_interval. Measured locally even with a co-located anvil.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger is the chain's block interval and the node's latency, not an excluded condition. A reviewer may argue that the recipe is documented only for local Anvil ('the same players against the real contracts, on a local Anvil chain') and that Arbitrum-like chains are unsupported anyway (their EVM block.number differs from the RPC block number); chains with matching block numbers and sub-second blocks exist.

2. Role: Support per AUDIT.md; section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'.
3. High/Medium cases: none of the listed cases in the honest role.

4. Critical in the stood-in role: R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks.' On a chain whose blocks come faster than one submit the honest operator never submits, so the honest claim loses every match by timeout (section 1 Completeness failure). Medium for the support component.

5. Low alternative: if the recipe's scope is read as local Anvil only, or the block interval vs latency is treated as deployment sizing (A7), it is Low (a liveness limit of a demo). Deciding facts: the chains the recipe claims to support and the latency budget A7 assumes for submission.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support standing in for R4) / Low (if the recipe is read as Anvil-only or the interval/latency ratio as deployment sizing)
candidates.threat_to_goal: The honest claim's responses are not submitted at all (fast chain) or only after a random multiple of the block interval, consuming its clock; a dishonest claim then wins by timeout.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r9/SUBJOURNAL/latency.lua against a private anvil 1.5.1 on this machine (local RPC, no network latency), 90 KB calldata transfers, a fresh job each time: manual mining, average submit 0.28 s (sign+decode 0.066 s); interval mining at 0.25 s blocks: 24 of 30 submits discarded as 'waiting' (6 published); at 1 s blocks: 2 of 20 discarded. A remote provider adds one round trip per RPC (about 10 sequential RPCs), and a leaf proof's eth_call/eth_estimateGas is heavier, so the discard rate on sub-second chains approaches 100%.
candidates.test_idea: Disposable anvil with manual mining. Wrap signer.sign (as prt-transactions-test.lua 365-378 already does) to mine one block during every signing, modelling a block interval shorter than one submit, and call submit for a job whose window [0, 1000) stays open. Required behavior: within a bounded number of attempts (for example 5) the job is published at nonce 0, since the window is open and the observation canonical at the new tip. On audit/prt2 it exits 1: every attempt returns waiting and nothing is stored or published.

not_covered: No run against geth or reth: the fee-cap refusal of candidate 1 was emulated by wrapping chain.publish with geth's checkTxFee rule (geth internal/ethapi SubmitTransaction, reth --rpc.txfeecap default 1.0 ether, from source knowledge); the real winLeafMatch eth_estimateGas for a 64 KiB input under the released constants was not measured (a gas burner reproduced about 6.3 M).

The bridge's job derivation (which jobs exist and their windows) was read only where it feeds the journal; persistently reverting but still-derived jobs (which would leave a stuck candidate unbumped and starve other due jobs of the same or a newer epoch) were reasoned about, not searched for exhaustively in Dave's contracts.

Starvation variants of the preference logic in methods:tick (a pending obsolete candidate while eligible[1] is awaiting observation, rejected at this tip, or blocked by insufficient funds or the fee ceiling, which blocks every other due job until the cancel is mined or the observation catches up): reasoned only; the delay is bounded by the observation lag or one cancel inclusion, so not reported (close to R1-A8-4).

Loss of the out-of-gas doubling when forget_settled forgets the job's OOG receipt before its retry (only when finality is not behind the dispute observation, for example dispute policy 'finalized'): reasoned, not reported, since no adversarial OOG at 2x estimate is known; EIP-7825's 2^24 per-transaction cap against 2 x exhausted gas likewise not reached.

Mempool eviction of an underpriced honest candidate during congestion (node holds none, fresh-fee candidates per bump interval) and its journal growth were reasoned only; reorg behaviour (R6-DYNBRIDGE-1 area), power-loss of journal.json, and multi-process use of one account were not re-tested.
prt-signer.lua was read (RLP fields, recovery id, cast decode checks) and exercised only through anvil; cast versions other than 1.5.1 and keystores with heavy scrypt parameters were not measured.
crisium end to end (several epochs' bridges sharing the account after a restart, remove_finished_epochs vs journal contexts) was reasoned from the code, not run with the player-restart runner.
